AI search for dentists

When a patient asks ChatGPT for a dentist, the practice it names is the one it's most sure about.

Getting your practice named by ChatGPT, Perplexity or Google's AI comes down to four things. Your details match everywhere. Each treatment has its own page. Those pages answer what patients ask in the first lines. And you've got a steady flow of real reviews. None of it is expensive. It's just done, or it isn't.

We do this for more than 100 dental clinics across Australia.

What we fix, in this order

  • 1. Your details, matching everywhere

    If your website says one phone number and a directory says another, an assistant is less sure which is right. Less sure means less likely to name you.

    We line up your practice name, address, phone, hours and treatments across your site, your Google listing and every directory you're on. It's the same job that lifts you on the map, so it pays twice.

  • 2. A page for every treatment

    An assistant can't recommend you for implants if your site only mentions them in a list.

    Implants, Invisalign, emergency, check-ups and whatever else you want more of each get a page that says plainly what it is, who it's for and how to book. Actual treatments and actual suburbs, in plain words.

  • 3. The answer in the first lines

    Patients don't type "dentist Caringbah" into ChatGPT. They ask whether they need a crown or a filling, or whether anyone can see them today.

    So we write your pages the way those questions get asked, with the answer up top. That's the part an assistant quotes. Everything is written to AHPRA's advertising guidelines, so nothing sets up expectations it shouldn't.

  • 4. The code underneath

    Structured data, or schema, is code on your site that spells out for machines what you do, where you are and when you're open.

    Most patients will never see it. Google and the AI tools read it on every visit.

  • 5. Real reviews, answered

    A steady flow of genuine reviews tells Google and the AI tools that your practice is active and trusted.

    We set up a simple way for patients to leave one and help you reply to them. They stay reviews, not testimonials, which keeps you inside AHPRA's rules.

  • 6. Checking what the assistants say

    This is the step most agencies skip.

    We ask the assistants the questions your patients ask, note whether you're named and how you're described, and fix the source when they get something wrong. Then we do it again, because the answers change.

Is this separate from SEO?

Straight answer: mostly the same work, written a bit differently.

An accurate map listing, a page per treatment, clean structure and real reviews help you on Google and in AI answers at the same time.

What changes is the writing. Pages need the answer up top, in the words a patient would use, so an assistant can lift it straight out. That's why AI search is part of how we do dental SEO, not an extra line on the invoice. How we do dental SEO.

What happens when you're named

Two or three names, and the patient rings more than one.

An assistant usually hands someone a short list. Whoever answers first tends to get the booking.

Every enquiry goes through SmileOX, our own lead platform. It replies to new enquiries in under 60 seconds, asks the questions your team would ask, and texts back the calls you miss. Getting named only matters if somebody answers. See how SmileOX works.

Straight answers

Questions dentists ask about AI search.

How do I get my dental practice to show up in ChatGPT?

Make it easy for the assistant to be sure about you. Your name, address, phone and treatments need to match everywhere you're listed, each treatment needs its own page that answers patient questions plainly in the first lines, the code on your site should spell out what you do and where, and you need a steady flow of real reviews.

Can you guarantee ChatGPT or Google's AI will recommend my practice?

No, and nobody honestly can. Nobody controls what an AI assistant says. What we can do is fix the things that make a practice easy to recommend, then check how the assistants describe you and keep fixing what they get wrong.

Is AI search different from dental SEO?

Less than people think. Most of the work is the same: an accurate map listing, a page for every treatment, clean technical structure and real reviews. The difference is in how the pages are written, with the answer up top where an assistant can quote it.

How long does it take?

The foundations go in during your first week with us, on day three. How quickly each assistant picks up the changes varies, so we won't put a date on it. We check how they describe you as we go.

Can AI answers about my practice break AHPRA rules?

The content we write for your site follows AHPRA's advertising guidelines, so what the assistants pick up from it does too. No testimonials about clinical care and nothing that sets up unreasonable expectations.

Will you do this for my competitor?

Not if they're a dental practice within 7km of you.
